<b>Гипофиз</b> — железа размером с горош: The pituitary is a pea-sized gland in the bony “Turkish saddle” (sella turcica) under the brain; the hypothalamus controls it. The anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) is a true gland: five cell types make six hormones. They are driven by releasing hormones (switch on) and inhibiting hormones (switch off), which small neurons of the arcuate, paraventricular and other hypothalamic nuclei release in the median eminence; short portal vessels carry them straight to the anterior-lobe cells. The posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) makes no hormones of its own: vasopressin and oxytocin are made by large neurons of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei, travel down their axons and wait in the terminals for a signal. Choose a hormone.
<b>Соматотропный гормон</b> (СТГ, гормон: Growth hormone (GH, somatotropin) is a protein of 191 amino acids made by somatotrophs, almost half of the anterior-lobe cells. GHRH switches it on, somatostatin switches it off, and ghrelin from the stomach also stimulates it. It is released in pulses, mostly during deep sleep. GH itself raises blood sugar and boosts fat breakdown (it is counter-regulatory to insulin), while bone growth runs through a messenger — IGF-1 from the liver. More in the “Growth hormone” mode.
<b>Пролактин</b> запускает и поддерживае: Prolactin starts and maintains milk production. It is the only anterior-lobe hormone that the hypothalamus mainly inhibits: dopamine (red stream, molecule on the right) keeps lactotrophs “on the brake” — so lactotrophs glow but release little. If a tumour compresses the pituitary stalk or drugs block dopamine (antipsychotics, metoclopramide), prolactin rises. Prolactinoma is the commonest hormone-secreting pituitary tumour: in women it disrupts the cycle and causes milk discharge, in men it lowers libido. It is treated with dopamine agonists (cabergoline), and the tumour often shrinks without surgery.
Кортикотрофы делают большой белок-предше: Corticotrophs make a large precursor protein, pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC, on the right). Convertase enzymes cut it into pieces: ACTH (drives the adrenal cortex — cortisol), melanocyte-stimulating hormones (MSH, skin pigmentation) and β-endorphin (the body’s own opioid). They are switched on by CRH from the paraventricular nucleus (together with vasopressin in stress); cortisol feeds back to inhibit both the hypothalamus and the pituitary. In Addison’s disease ACTH is very high and the skin darkens: the start of the ACTH molecule matches α-MSH, and excess ACTH itself acts on MSH receptors (MC1R) in melanocytes. A corticotroph adenoma causes Cushing’s disease. See the “Adrenal glands” topic.
<b>Тиреотропный гормон</b> (ТТГ) — глико: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is a glycoprotein of two subunits: α is the same as in LH, FSH and hCG, β is its own. It is switched on by TRH (just three amino acids, molecule on the right; made by small neurons of the paraventricular nucleus) and switched off by somatostatin and the thyroid hormones themselves. TSH is the most sensitive test of thyroid function. See the “Thyroid hormones” topic.
Гонадотрофы делают <b>лютеинизирующий</b: Gonadotrophs make luteinizing (LH) and follicle-stimulating (FSH) hormones. They are switched on by GnRH, but only when it arrives in pulses — about once every 1–2 hours (see the flashes of the stream). Continuous GnRH, by contrast, shuts gonadotrophs down within a couple of weeks — this is how GnRH analogues treat prostate cancer. In men LH drives testosterone synthesis and FSH sperm maturation; in women they drive follicle maturation and ovulation. See the “Sex hormones” topic.
<b>Вазопрессин</b> (антидиуретический го: Vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone, ADH) is a 9-amino-acid peptide with a disulfide bridge (molecule on the right). It is made by neurons of the supraoptic (mostly) and paraventricular nuclei; granules travel down the axons into the posterior lobe. The release signals are a rise in blood osmolality (osmoreceptors sense a 1–2% shift) and a large fall in blood pressure or volume. In the kidney, via the V2 receptor, it inserts water channels — aquaporins — and urine becomes concentrated (the “Vasopressin and water” mode); via the V1 receptor it constricts vessels. Alcohol inhibits vasopressin release — hence frequent urination.
<b>Окситоцин</b> — тоже нонапептид; от в: Oxytocin is also a nonapeptide; it differs from vasopressin by two amino acids (molecule on the right). It is made mainly in the paraventricular nucleus. It is released reflexly: when the cervix is stretched in labour (contractions boost release, release boosts contractions — positive feedback) and during breastfeeding, when milk is squeezed out of the alveoli (the “let-down reflex”). Synthetic oxytocin is given to induce labour and to stop bleeding after birth. In the brain it takes part in attachment and trust.
Клетка <b>собирательной трубки</b> почки: A collecting duct cell of the kidney. Above is the tubule lumen (future urine), below is blood. Vasopressin binds the V2 receptor, cAMP rises via the G protein, protein kinase A phosphorylates aquaporin-2 (blue), and vesicles carrying it fuse with the urine-side membrane. Water follows the osmotic gradient from urine through the cell into blood (through the always-open aquaporins 3 and 4, green) — urine becomes concentrated. Without vasopressin aquaporins return inside the cell, the membrane becomes water-tight and urine is dilute. Normally there are 1–2 L of urine a day (1 second = 4 hours).
Человек <b>без доступа к воде</b>. Вода: A person without access to water. Water is lost with breath, sweat and urine, blood becomes more concentrated and osmolality rises — the hypothalamus switches on thirst and vasopressin release. All aquaporins are in the membrane, urine is under a litre a day, dark and concentrated (up to 1200 mOsm/kg — four times more concentrated than blood). The kidneys can only save water — it can be replaced only by drinking.
<b>Центральный несахарный диабет</b>: ва: Central diabetes insipidus: there is no vasopressin (injury or tumour near the pituitary, surgery, sometimes autoimmune damage). Aquaporins are not inserted, and the kidney excretes up to 15–20 litres of dilute urine a day. The person is constantly thirsty: drinking freely keeps blood sodium near the upper limit of normal; without access to water they dehydrate quickly.
<b>Нефрогенный несахарный диабет</b>: ва: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: there is plenty of vasopressin, but the kidney does not hear it — a mutation of the V2 receptor (X-linked) or aquaporin-2, or a drug side effect (lithium salts). Blood hormone levels are high, yet there are no aquaporins in the membrane. Desmopressin does not help.
<b>Синдром неадекватной секреции АДГ</b>: Syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH): vasopressin is released without need — with tumours (especially small-cell lung cancer), lung and brain disease, and some drugs. The kidney retains water and blood is diluted: osmolality and sodium fall (hyponatremia), while urine stays concentrated. Severe hyponatremia causes brain swelling: headache, confusion, seizures.
Человек пьёт — осмоляльность возвращаетс: The person drinks — osmolality returns to normal, vasopressin falls, some aquaporins leave the membrane, and the kidneys excrete the extra water.
<b>Десмопрессин</b> — синтетический анал: Desmopressin is a synthetic vasopressin analogue: it acts only on the V2 receptor (hardly constricts vessels) and lasts longer. Tablets or a nasal spray bring aquaporins back into the membrane — urine is again about 1–1.5 litres. No more drinking than usual is needed.
<b>Тиазидные диуретики</b> парадоксально: Thiazide diuretics paradoxically reduce urine volume: a small sodium loss increases salt and water reabsorption in the proximal tubule, so less fluid reaches the collecting ducts. Together with a low-salt, low-protein diet, urine volume roughly halves, but does not return to normal.
<b>Лечение СНСАДГ</b>: ограничить питьё: Treating SIADH: restrict fluids to 0.8–1 L a day and treat the cause; in severe cases — vaptans (V2 receptor blockers) and careful infusion of hypertonic (3%) NaCl (ordinary saline can even worsen hyponatremia). Sodium is raised no faster than 8–10 mmol/L per day — otherwise osmotic demyelination occurs in the brain.
<b>Гормон роста</b> выделяется импульсам: Growth hormone is released in pulses — mostly at night, in deep sleep, and in adolescence. On its own it raises blood sugar and burns fat, while it tells bones to grow mainly through a messenger — insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), made in response to GH by the liver (and the tissues themselves). IGF-1 makes cartilage cells divide in the growth plates at the ends of long bones (glowing). By 16–18 years, under sex hormones, the plates close — after that a person no longer grows taller. Time runs by itself; the height chart is in the corner.
<b>Дефицит гормона роста</b> у ребёнка (: Growth hormone deficiency in a child (congenital or after a tumour or radiotherapy): up to one year the child grows almost normally, then growth velocity halves while body proportions are preserved. Untreated adult height is about 130–140 cm. Intelligence is not affected (unlike congenital hypothyroidism).
<b>Гигантизм</b>: аденома из соматотрофо: Gigantism: a somatotroph adenoma appeared in childhood (here at age 8), while the growth plates were open. IGF-1 is three times above normal, bones grow in length, height exceeds 2 metres, and the plates close later than usual. The tumour may press on the optic chiasm — the outer visual fields are lost.
<b>Акромегалия</b>: аденома появилась у: Acromegaly: the adenoma appeared in an adult (here at 20), when the growth plates were already closed. Bones no longer grow in length, but the hands, feet, lower jaw, nose, tongue and internal organs thicken and enlarge. The disease progresses slowly and is often noticed after 5–10 years — when rings and shoes no longer fit. It is dangerous because of diabetes, hypertension and heart disease.
<b>Рекомбинантный гормон роста</b> — уко: Recombinant growth hormone — daily injections until the growth plates close. Treatment started at age 4: the child “catches up” with peers and reaches almost normal height. Growth hormone used to be extracted from the pituitaries of the deceased — until it turned out that this transmits the prion Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease; since 1985 only the genetically engineered hormone is used.
<b>Лечение</b>: удаление аденомы через н: Treatment: removal of the adenoma through the nose (transsphenoidal surgery), somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide) or the GH receptor blocker pegvisomant. After surgery at 11, IGF-1 normalizes and the child then grows at the usual rate.
<b>Лечение акромегалии</b> — то же, что: Treating acromegaly is the same as gigantism: surgery, octreotide, pegvisomant. After surgery at 22, IGF-1 normalizes, soft-tissue growth stops and partly reverses, but the bone changes remain.
Участок мозга размером с ноготь и железа: A patch of brain the size of a fingernail and a pea-sized gland control growth, water, stress, metabolism, reproduction and milk.
\n <div><h2>Гипоталамо-гипофизарная:
The hypothalamic–pituitary system

The hypothalamus links the nervous system to the endocrine system. Its parvocellular neurons release releasing and inhibiting hormones into the portal system: thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH), corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH), gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), growth hormone–releasing hormone (GHRH), somatostatin and dopamine (prolactin-inhibiting factor). Magnocellular neurons of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesize vasopressin and oxytocin together with neurophysin proteins; the hormones are stored in axon terminals in the posterior lobe.

Anterior-lobe hormones

  • Proteins and peptides: GH (191 amino acids), prolactin (199), ACTH (39) — from pro-opiomelanocortin together with MSH and β-endorphin.
  • Glycoproteins of α and β subunits: TSH, LH, FSH (the α subunit is also shared with human chorionic gonadotropin).
  • Feedback: target-gland hormones (cortisol, T₄, sex steroids) and IGF-1 inhibit the hypothalamus and pituitary.

Mechanism of action

TSH, LH, FSH, ACTH, vasopressin (V2) — G protein–coupled receptors (cAMP); vasopressin (V1) and oxytocin — via phospholipase C and Ca²⁺; GH and prolactin — receptors coupled to JAK tyrosine kinases.

Diseases

  • Pituitary adenomas: prolactinoma, somatotropinoma (gigantism, acromegaly), corticotropinoma (Cushing’s disease); large tumours compress the optic chiasm.
  • Hypopituitarism (for example, after childbirth with heavy blood loss — Sheehan syndrome).
  • Diabetes insipidus (central, nephrogenic), syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion.

Simplifications

  • The hypothalamus, pituitary and kidney cell are diagrams, not to scale; the number of anterior-lobe cells is arbitrary, the ratio of types approximate.
  • Vasopressin, oxytocin, TRH and dopamine molecules are built from their chemical formulas. The V2 receptor is shown with the structure of another receptor of the same family (β2-adrenergic receptor with G protein, PDB 3SN6).
  • The water and growth models are simplified; time is accelerated, the growth curve is the median for boys.

Keys

  • 1–3 mode
  • R · N
<b>β-клетка</b> островка Лангерганса — д: The β-cell of the islet of Langerhans is a sugar sensor. Glucose enters through the GLUT2 transporter (in humans mostly GLUT1), glucokinase phosphorylates it (its Km is high, so its rate rises with blood glucose), and glycolysis and mitochondria produce ATP. ATP closes the K-ATP channel (a pore of Kir6.2 plus regulatory SUR1): potassium stops leaving, the membrane depolarizes, Ca²⁺ channels open (calcium ions are green), and calcium triggers granule fusion with the membrane — insulin enters the blood together with C-peptide cut from proinsulin (in equal amounts — which is why C-peptide is used to judge the body’s own secretion). Try different glucose levels and watch the potential on the chart.
Натощак (около 5 ммоль/л) АТФ мало, K-АТ: Fasting (about 5 mmol/L) there is little ATP, K-ATP channels are mostly open, the membrane sits near −65 mV — the cell is silent and releases only a little basal insulin.
После еды глюкозы 10 ммоль/л: АТФ много,: After a meal glucose is 10 mmol/L: plenty of ATP, K-ATP channels closed, the membrane rises above threshold, bursts of action potentials run, calcium enters — granules release insulin en masse.
Глюкозы 3 ммоль/л — секреция почти выклю: At 3 mmol/L glucose secretion is almost off, so the cell does not stop the liver from raising sugar. This is how the β-cell protects against hypoglycemia.
<b>Сульфонилмочевина</b> (глибенкламид,: A sulfonylurea (glibenclamide, molecule by the channel) binds SUR1 and closes the K-ATP channel regardless of glucose. So it releases insulin even when sugar is low — hypoglycemia is the main risk of these tablets. Choose “Low: 3” — secretion continues. The same channels are mutated in neonatal diabetes, and such children are treated with tablets instead of injections. With GLP-1 agonists the risk of hypoglycemia is even higher: since the channel is already closed, the cAMP boost works even at low sugar — so the sulfonylurea dose is reduced. Turn both on.
<b>GLP-1</b> — гормон-инкретин из кишечн: GLP-1 is an incretin hormone from the gut. Through its receptor (purple) and cAMP it amplifies insulin release, but only when glucose is high: at “Low: 3” there is no effect, so GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide) on their own hardly ever cause hypoglycemia. They also slow stomach emptying, reduce appetite and glucagon release.
<b>Сутки здорового человека</b> (1 секун: A day of a healthy person (1 second = 1 hour, dots at the bottom of the chart — meals). After breakfast, lunch and dinner, glucose from the gut raises sugar to 7–8 mmol/L, the pancreas releases insulin (blue streams), the liver, muscles and fat take up glucose, and within 2 hours sugar returns to 4–6. At night the liver (orange stream) releases a little glucose from glycogen, while basal insulin keeps it from releasing too much.
<b>Диабет 1 типа</b>: иммунная система р: Type 1 diabetes: the immune system has destroyed the β-cells — C-peptide is almost zero, there is no insulin. Sugar rises to 20–30 mmol/L (how exactly — see the “Glycogen and blood sugar” topic), glucose spills into urine and drags water with it. Without insulin fat breaks down unchecked and the liver makes ketone bodies (red glow): ketones above 3 mmol/L and blood pH below 7.3 mean diabetic ketoacidosis — nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, acetone breath, deep laboured (Kussmaul) breathing, dehydration, confusion. This is an emergency: it is treated with intravenous insulin, fluids and potassium.
<b>Инсулинотерапия</b> заменяет поджелуд: Insulin therapy replaces the pancreas: long-acting (basal) insulin once a day keeps the liver in check, short-acting insulin is given before every meal (injections into subcutaneous fat). Sugar stays mostly in the target range; doses are calculated from meal carbohydrates and glucose readings (today often with a sensor and pump). Too much insulin means hypoglycemia, so it is important to know its signs.
Type 2 diabetes is 90% of all cases. Tissues respond poorly to insulin (insulin resistance — especially with excess visceral fat), the liver releases extra glucose, and the β-cells gradually wear out and cannot cope with the higher load. Sugar stays high all day. Treatment is based on diet, exercise and weight loss; then tablets and injections. Try the drugs one by one and together.
<b>Метформин</b> — первое лекарство при: Metformin is the first-line drug for type 2 diabetes. Above all it slows glucose release from the liver (gluconeogenesis; partly via the enzyme AMPK) and slightly improves insulin sensitivity. It does not cause hypoglycemia by itself and does not add weight.
<b>Глифлозины</b> (дапаглифлозин, эмпагл: Gliflozins (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) block the SGLT2 transporter in the kidney tubules — the renal glucose threshold drops to about 5 mmol/L, and 40–80 g of glucose a day leave with urine (yellow stream to the bladder). Sugar falls independently of insulin; they are proven to protect the heart and kidneys.
<b>Лираглутид / семаглутид</b> — агонист: Liraglutide / semaglutide are GLP-1 receptor agonists: they amplify insulin release only when sugar is high, suppress glucagon, slow stomach emptying (lower post-meal peaks) and reduce appetite — helping weight loss.
<b>Инсулин</b> при диабете 2 типа добавл: Insulin is added in type 2 diabetes when tablets are no longer enough: usually starting with one injection of long-acting insulin a day — it lowers fasting sugar.
<b>Гликирование</b> — глюкоза сама, без: Glycation — glucose attaches to free amino groups of proteins by itself, without an enzyme. The aldehyde group of glucose forms a Schiff base with NH₂ (reversible — glucose can leave), which rearranges into a stable Amadori product. This is how HbA1c forms — hemoglobin with glucose on the N-terminal valine of the β chain (orange dots — glycated sites; lysines are glycated too). A red cell lives about 120 days, so HbA1c reflects average sugar over 2–3 months: normal is below 6%, the usual target in diabetes is below 7%. Below — 100 hemoglobin molecules, the orange ones are glycated.
Средний сахар около 7,5 ммоль/л — HbA1c: Average sugar about 7.5 mmol/L — HbA1c about 6.3%. This is good control: the risk of complications is low. Note the chart: HbA1c changes slowly, weeks after sugar changes.
Средний сахар около 12 ммоль/л — HbA1c о: Average sugar about 12 mmol/L — HbA1c about 9%. Proteins all over the body are glycated — collagen, lens proteins, vessel walls, the basement membranes of kidney glomeruli. Over time Amadori products give rise to irreversible advanced glycation end products (AGEs): proteins cross-link, tissues lose elasticity, inflammation starts. In the lens (on the right) glucose is converted by aldose reductase into sorbitol via the polyol pathway; sorbitol barely leaves the cells, draws in water, and the fibres swell and cloud — diabetic cataract. Aldose reductase works only at high sugar (its Km is high) and uses up NADPH — the cell runs short of reduced glutathione and oxidative stress rises. The same pathway harms nerves and the retina. That is why diabetes damages small vessels (eyes, kidneys, nerves) and large ones (heart attack, stroke).
Одна клетка поджелудочной меряет сахар к: A single pancreatic cell measures blood sugar to a fraction of a millimole — and half a billion people live with diabetes when this sensor breaks.
\n <div><h2>Инсулин</h2>\n <:
Insulin

A protein of two chains (A — 21 and B — 30 amino acids) joined by two disulfide bridges. It is made as preproinsulin; in the granules C-peptide is cut out of proinsulin — it is measured to assess the body’s own secretion in patients on injections. In the granules insulin is stored as zinc hexamers.

Secretion

  • Glucose → GLUT2 (in humans mostly GLUT1) → glucokinase (sensor) → ATP/ADP ↑ → closure of K-ATP channels → depolarization → voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels → exocytosis.
  • Enhanced by: the incretins GLP-1 and GIP (cAMP), amino acids, parasympathetic nerves; inhibited by: adrenaline (α₂), somatostatin.
  • Two phases: rapid (ready granules at the membrane) and slow.

Action

Receptor tyrosine kinase → IRS → PI3K → Akt: GLUT4 to the membrane of muscle and fat, synthesis of glycogen, fat and protein; inhibition of gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, lipolysis and ketogenesis. Glucagon, adrenaline, cortisol and GH are counter-regulatory hormones.

Diabetes

  • Type 1 — autoimmune destruction of β-cells, absolute insulin deficiency; risk of ketoacidosis.
  • Type 2 — insulin resistance + progressive β-cell failure; hyperosmolar state in the elderly.
  • Gestational, MODY (monogenic, e.g. glucokinase mutations), secondary.
  • Diagnosis: fasting glucose ≥ 7.0 mmol/L, 2 hours after a glucose load ≥ 11.1, HbA1c ≥ 6.5%.
  • Complications: microangiopathy (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy), macroangiopathy, diabetic foot.

Simplifications

  • The cell, granules and channels are diagrams, not to scale; glucose, glibenclamide and sorbitol molecules are built from their chemical formulas; hemoglobin is a real structure (PDB 4HHB).
  • The day model is simplified, doses and drug responses are approximate; 1 second = 1 hour. Average sugar is converted to HbA1c with the ADAG study formula.
  • The number of glycated sites on the molecule is shown schematically — it reflects the HbA1c level, not the actual fraction.

Keys

  • 1–3 mode
  • R · N
<b>Половые стероиды</b> делаются из холе: Sex steroids are made from cholesterol. CYP11A1 in mitochondria cuts off the side chain to give pregnenolone; then CYP17 (17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase) removes two more carbons, and 3β-HSD and 17β-HSD finish the job to testosterone (in humans androgens are made mainly via DHEA; the left part of the pathway is the same as in the adrenal cortex). In men 95% of testosterone is made by the Leydig cells of the testis in response to LH. In target tissues (prostate, skin, hair follicles) 5α-reductase converts it into dihydrotestosterone (DHT), 2–3 times more potent; a small part is converted by aromatase (in fat tissue) into estradiol — men need it for bone and for closing the growth plates.
В яичнике работают <b>две клетки, два го: The ovary works on two cells, two hormones. Theca cells, driven by LH, make androstenedione from cholesterol (they lack aromatase); it passes to neighbouring granulosa cells, where FSH-driven aromatase (CYP19) converts androgens into estrogens: androstenedione → estrone, testosterone → estradiol (the main estrogen). After ovulation the corpus luteum makes a lot of progesterone. Aromatase removes carbon C19 and makes ring A aromatic — that is why estrogens have a phenol-like ring (with an OH group).
В яичнике до менопаузы летрозол работает: In the ovary before menopause letrozole works differently: estradiol falls, the pituitary responds with more FSH — this is how letrozole is used to induce ovulation (for example, in polycystic ovary syndrome). That is why, in breast cancer before menopause, it is combined with ovarian suppression.
<b>Летрозол</b> (и анастрозол) блокируют: Letrozole (and anastrozole) block aromatase: estrogens almost disappear. This treats hormone-dependent breast cancer in postmenopausal women, when estrogens are made only by aromatase in fat tissue. Androgens accumulate and bones lose calcium (osteoporosis must be monitored).
<b>Финастерид</b> блокирует 5α-редуктазу: Finasteride blocks 5α-reductase (type 2): DHT falls by about 70%, while testosterone even rises slightly. The prostate shrinks — it is used for benign prostatic hyperplasia, and at a low dose for male-pattern baldness. Boys with congenital 5α-reductase deficiency are born with underdeveloped external genitalia — their formation needs DHT specifically.
<b>Ось гипоталамус — гипофиз — яички.</b: The hypothalamic–pituitary–testicular axis. The hypothalamus releases GnRH in pulses (the stream flashes), the pituitary responds with LH and FSH. LH drives testosterone synthesis in Leydig cells; FSH, together with high testosterone inside the testis, supports sperm maturation in Sertoli cells (which also make inhibin, inhibiting FSH). Testosterone feeds back to inhibit the hypothalamus and pituitary (red arrow), builds muscle and bone, and drives hair growth and the voice.
<b>Анаболические стероиды</b> (тестостер: Anabolic steroids (testosterone and its derivatives in high doses): blood androgens are several times above normal — muscles grow faster. But feedback silences the hypothalamus and pituitary: LH and FSH are almost zero, the testes stop making their own testosterone — inside the testis it is dozens of times below normal, the testes shrink, spermatogenesis stops — infertility, sometimes for years. Excess androgens are aromatized to estradiol — breast tissue grows (gynecomastia). Also: acne, baldness, raised hematocrit, blood pressure and LDL (while HDL falls), liver damage (with oral forms), mood swings.
<b>Вторичный гипогонадизм</b>: гипоталам: Secondary hypogonadism: the hypothalamus or pituitary does not release gonadotropins (tumour, injury, Kallmann syndrome — GnRH neurons failed to migrate to the hypothalamus, usually with loss of smell). LH and FSH are low, testosterone is low, the testes are small, puberty does not occur. It is treated with testosterone (for sex characteristics) or gonadotropins / pulsatile GnRH (if fertility is needed).
<b>Ось гипоталамус — гипофиз — яичники.<: The hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis. FSH grows the follicle, and the granulosa makes more and more estradiol. Normally estradiol inhibits the pituitary, but when it stays high for about two days the feedback switches to positive — the LH surge on day 14 triggers ovulation (flash). The corpus luteum makes progesterone and estradiol, then breaks down if there is no pregnancy. More in the “Menstrual cycle” topic in the “Body” section.
<b>Комбинированные контрацептивы</b> — э: Combined contraceptives — ethinylestradiol (an estrogen resistant to breakdown in the liver) + a progestin (for example, levonorgestrel). A constant hormone level keeps feedback negative: FSH does not grow a follicle, no LH surge — no ovulation. The progestin also thickens cervical mucus. The body’s own estradiol is low, but ethinylestradiol from the pill does its job.
<b>Менопауза</b> (в среднем в 51 год): ф: Menopause (on average at 51): the ovarian follicles have run out, estradiol and inhibin fall — there is no brake, and FSH and LH are very high (the diagnosis is made after a year without periods; FSH is checked in unclear cases). Without estrogens — hot flushes, dry mucous membranes, bone loss (osteoporosis), higher risk of atherosclerosis. Hormone replacement therapy relieves symptoms and is prescribed individually.
<b>Тест на беременность</b> — иммунохром: A pregnancy test is an immunochromatographic strip. Urine soaks in and flows to the right. The conjugate zone holds antibodies to the β subunit of hCG (purple) labelled with gold nanoparticles (red-purple). The test line carries antibodies to the α subunit, the control line carries antibodies against the conjugate antibodies themselves. Without hCG the conjugates have nothing to hold on to at the test line — they pass on and colour only the control line: the test worked, the result is negative. Above — the real structure of an IgG antibody (PDB 1IGT) and a diagram of hCG.
<b>ХГЧ</b> (хорионический гонадотропин): hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is made by the embryo’s trophoblast after implantation — 6–10 days after conception. It resembles LH (shared α subunit) and acts on the same receptor: it keeps the corpus luteum from breaking down, so it goes on making progesterone until the placenta takes over by gestational week 7–9. hCG doubles every 2–3 days. An hCG molecule with a conjugate attached (an “antibody — hCG — antibody” sandwich) is held at the test line — a second line appears. At 25 mIU/mL the line is still faint.
На 8–10-й акушерской неделе (6–8 недель: At gestational weeks 8–10 (6–8 weeks after conception) hCG peaks — up to 100,000 mIU/mL and more: the test line is bright at once. Rapid tests for COVID, flu and other antigens work the same way. A blood β-hCG test is more precise and gives the amount: from how fast hCG rises a doctor tells a normal pregnancy from an ectopic or failed one. Very high hCG occurs in multiple pregnancy and molar pregnancy; hCG is also a marker of some testicular tumours.

Sex hormones

Androgens (C19): testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, DHEA (mostly from the adrenals). Estrogens (C18, aromatic ring A): estradiol, estrone, estriol (from the placenta in pregnancy). Progestins (C21): progesterone. All are made from cholesterol; the key regulated step is delivery of cholesterol into the mitochondrion by the StAR protein.

Transport and action

In blood they are bound to sex hormone–binding globulin (SHBG) and albumin. They act through nuclear receptors (AR, ERα/β, PR): the hormone–receptor complex binds DNA and changes transcription. A mutation of the androgen receptor causes androgen insensitivity syndrome.

Regulation

  • Pulsatile GnRH → LH, FSH; continuous GnRH suppresses them (GnRH analogues in prostate cancer, endometriosis, precocious puberty).
  • Negative feedback by steroids and inhibin; in women at mid-cycle — positive (the LH surge).

hCG

A glycoprotein of an α subunit (shared with LH, FSH, TSH) and a β subunit (its own — this is what tests detect). It maintains the corpus luteum and, in a male fetus, stimulates Leydig cells.

Simplifications

  • Steroid and drug molecules are built from their chemical formulas; antibodies are the real IgG structure (PDB 1IGT), hCG is a two-subunit diagram.
  • Hormone levels are typical values, not the reference ranges of a particular lab; time is accelerated (1 s ≈ 1 day of the cycle).
  • The test strip, body and organs are diagrams, not to scale.
